en: XX. The Chapter on the Exposition of the Four Yugas. Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the four yugas according to their measurement.
Now, therefore,
by means of which [knowledge], as soon as it is understood, the swift calculation (śīghrāṅka) arises through measurement. (20.1)
Twenty-eight thousand and seventeen hundred thousand— this is declared to be their measurement; it is described as being fashioned by the practitioner.
The junction between the Kṛta and Tretā ages consists of exactly eight thousand years;
[the Kṛta age] lasts for twelve hundred thousand and eighty-four thousand years.
The Tretā Kalpa is thus described and known by the wise;
the junction between the Tretā and Dvāpara ages is ordained to last for six thousand years.
In the Dvāpara age, sixty-four thousand and eight hundred thousand [verses] are studied.
It was condensed across all the scriptures during the duration of the Dvāpara age.
The junction between the Dvāpara and Kali ages consists of exactly four thousand [years]; thus,
thirty-two thousand and four hundred [years] are prescribed.
The conjunction produced by the Kali [age] is four thousand in numerical figures.
The pair of these has been declared; it is accomplished, there is no doubt in this. || 20.7 ||
I shall tell you, O Lord, the four cultivations of the continents: Pūrvavideha, Uttarakuru, and likewise Aparagodānīya. (20.8)
[Regarding *apara*: emended to *apara*, [the manuscript A reads] *avara*.
These three continents are established as the stage of fruition (*phalabhūmi*).
[Regarding *dvīpānām*: ] emended to *dvīpānām*, [the manuscript A reads] *dvīpānā*.
Born in the auspicious Jambūdvīpa, one is established upon the ground of accomplishment.
For one born in the triple-continent [Trayadvīpa], there arises the fruit of merit from sacred fords;
in Jambūdvīpa, both spiritual accomplishments (siddhi) and liberation (mokṣa) are attained.
These lead to accomplishment and liberation; indeed, the designation "islands" for these was spoken by a previous Buddha. || 20.10 ||
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the Exposition of the Four Yugas.
